title: Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retries
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Users are building flows that invoke multiple tools per user request (data enrichment, external lookups, and action execution). The existing tool-calling execution path serializes tool invocations and has brittle retry semantics and awkward result injection into model context. This PR improves ergonomics by adding first-class support for parallel multi-tool execution, deterministic result injection semantics that preserve streaming behavior, and robust retry/backoff with idempotency keys.

What changed: refactored the tool executor to support a parallel fan-out mode with a configurable concurrency cap, introduced an injection controller that materializes tool outputs into the chat/structured output stream while preserving token ordering guarantees, and implemented retry semantics with per-tool idempotency and exponential backoff. The OpenAI-compatibility handler now accepts a new tool_calling.options object (backwards compatible) to opt into parallel mode and retry policies. Added comprehensive unit and integration tests and updated docs and SDK surfaces.

Checklist:
- [x] Parallel tool executor with concurrency controls and cancellation support
- [x] Tool result injection controller for streaming + structured outputs
- [x] Retry/backoff and idempotency key propagation
- [x] OpenAI-compat layer parameter plumbing and compatibility tests
- [x] SDK helpers (Python/TS) and examples updated
- [x] Docs: tool-calling guide updated with examples and migration notes

Testing: Unit tests cover executor state transitions, injection ordering, and retry paths. Integration tests include a multi-tool example with a mocked external service to simulate transient failures and validate idempotent retry. Load tests were run on perf-canary to validate latency impact at concurrency 16. CI had one flaky e2e test that was rerun and passed.

Rollout: Feature is gated behind a runtime flag tool_calling.parallel_enabled (false by default). The OpenAI-compat layer exposes options but defaults to previous serial behavior. Recommend canary rollout to 10% of traffic and monitoring for increased tail latency metrics (RPS, p95/p99, tool_executor.retries, streaming_resends).

Notes on backwards compatibility: Defaults preserve existing behavior; new options are additive. SDKs include convenience wrappers for constructing the new options. No breaking client API changes expected.
commit_summary: Refactor: introduce ParallelToolExecutor with concurrency limits and cancellation
feat(openai-compat): add tool_calling.options plumbing and migration shim
feat(executor): implement result injection controller and streaming adapters
fix(retries): add idempotency key propagation and exponential backoff with jitter
test: add unit/integration tests for parallel flows and retry semantics
docs: update docs/tool-calling.md and examples in sdk repos
changed_files: packages/redwood/src/runtime/tool_executor.py - core parallel executor and injection controller
packages/redwood-sdk-python/redwood/tooling.py - helper to build options and idempotency wrapper
packages/redwood/tests/test_tool_calls.py - new unit tests for state transitions
packages/redwood-integration-tests/test_multi_tool_flow.py - integration test with flaky service mock
perf-canary/configs/multi-tool-load.yml - load test config used for perf validation
packages/redwood-console/src/components/ToolCallPanel.jsx - small UI update to toggle parallel mode
review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Request changes - ensure cancellation semantics are well-defined when one tool fails but others are still running; also add metrics for concurrent in-flight tool calls.
Aisha Patel: Reply - added cancellation propagation and a new metric tool_executor.in_flight_count; updated tests to assert cancellation behavior.
Leah Kim: Comment - can we avoid increasing p99 under high concurrency? Suggest a configurable concurrency cap and default to 8.
Aisha Patel: Reply - added a runtime config and defaulted to 8; added notes in rollout guidance and unit tests for concurrency cap enforcement.
Omar Hassan: Approve with comment - left one nit about variable naming in handler.ts, addressed in follow-up commit.
CI Bot: e2e test flaky on first run (timeout), reran and passed; all checks green before merge.
release_notes: Add parallel multi-tool execution mode for tool-calling with deterministic result injection and robust retry/idempotency support. Backwards compatible and gated by runtime flag. SDKs and docs updated.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Defaults preserve serial execution; OpenAI-compat layer exposes new options but maintains previous behavior when not set. No breaking changes in public API.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for executor state, injection ordering, retries; integration test simulates transient external failures and validates idempotency; perf-canary validated no regression at default concurrency cap 8.
migration_guidance: Clients wishing to opt into parallel execution should set tool_calling.options.parallel=true and provide an idempotency_key per logical user request. Start with concurrency target 4-8 and monitor p95/p99 latency and tool_executor.retries metrics.
notes_for_ops: Gate enabled by runtime flag tool_calling.parallel_enabled=false. Rollout with feature flag, monitor tool_executor.in_flight_count, tool_executor.retries, streaming_resend_count, request_latency.p99. If tail latency increases, reduce concurrency cap or revert flag.
